chapter_theme: Conquest of bindu (விந்து ஜயம்) and the practice of union governed by the breath (போக சரவோட்டம்): the yogi turns desire back to the root and, raising the inner fire, drinks the nectar of the moon instead of losing bindu; where union with a woman happens, it is timed by the lunar days and the breath and held so that bindu is not spilled. Kept bindu gives breath, strength, siddhi and the state of Sivoham.
structure_note: Turning from women and the need for grace (1937, 1938); the rite of union, its days, breath and conception (1939 to 1945); the seed and its sower (1946, 1947); bindu kept, burnt upward and turned to nectar (1948 to 1966, with 1953 on seeing women as death and 1955, 1960, 1961 on union without loss); the teaching, mantra and Sivoham (1967 to 1971); the place of knowing and the elements in the body (1972 to 1974).

1937.reading: The yogi who leaves without looking at the women he sees, kindles a fire so the reflecting heart melts, lays waste the eye's desire and joins it at the root, is the Siva-yogi.
1937.nuance: பார்க்கின்ற opens lines 1 and 3: the women seen and the eye that sees. மூலத்தே சேர்க்கின்ற is taken as turning the force of desire back to the muladhara, the root centre, rather than suppressing it; the verse does not name what is joined.

1938.reading: Without grace Siva-yoga does not stay; one who harbours lust and its kin lives in fear; if the will to rule stays, the body is ruined, and in the flesh, if the life is not tended among these, it dies.
1938.nuance: தானே opens three lines. அதிகாரம் may be worldly power, the ego's claim to command, or in Siddhanta the stage of the soul's bondage; சடம் is the inert body. The verse puts grace before technique in a chapter mostly of technique.

1939.reading: If they wish to go into a woman's power, then of the two fortnights, in the waxing one, eight days are for pleasure; and in the waning one it is the sixth from the first day.
1939.nuance: மாயாள் may simply be 'the woman' or carry the sense of maya, the one who deludes. மேல்பனி மூன்றிரண்டு and the day counts are obscure; the verse fixes lunar days for union, as in the traditional rules for conception, but the exact days cannot be fixed from the text.

1940.reading: Apart from the sixth, fifth and eleventh, those who want a love other than the common way should, after the woman's flowering, take the twenty-one days in which it rises, and do it at the time when the sixth rises highest.
1940.nuance: பூவரில் is taken as the woman's menses. சகமார்க்கம் (the common way) and the numbers are obscure; the verse continues 1939's calendar.

1941.reading: When it is done, the holy fourth muhurta, the time when the kala shoots, when the moon and sun breaths weaken, run there and act by the treatise's good way; leaving right and left, release.
1941.nuance: இந்து பருதிகால் are the moon and sun breaths, the left and right channels. வலம் இடம் தீர்ந்து (leaving right and left) is taken as the breath moving in the central channel. What is released (விடுக்க) is not said; the next verses suggest it is not bindu itself.

1942.reading: Release, and see: one who stays unshaken as the senses strain, as the five-times-five draw near, letting go all clinging to the woman of desire, holding the fierce breath and the faculties to the mind.
1942.nuance: ஐஐந்து may be the twenty-five tattvas or five times the five senses. கடுங்கால் (fierce wind) is taken as the breath held hard. The verse asks for detachment in the very act, not abstention from it.

1943.reading: With words like 'nature I have taken, goodness, tender one, form of old, coral-lipped, firm-breasted', when the moment of close release comes, see the faculty you have seen go within, then release.
1943.nuance: The first lines are a lover's endearments. கண்ட கரணம் உட் செல்ல (the faculty seen going within) is taken as the breath or the bindu drawn inward before release; the sense is that the yogi keeps the inner turning even at the climax.

1944.reading: After release, in the rules of conception, consider the times that came into play and look to the life span bound, the day of death, low qualities and high, thinking 'this is the way it went'.
1944.nuance: The verse seems to say that the time of union fixes the child's length of life, death day and character, as in the astrological lore of conception. சீர்ப்பட்ட நெறி may be 'the proper way' or 'the way it turned out'.

1945.reading: Having looked to this, free of the world's spread and gaining form, keeping away from the woman, and even if one parts and keeps apart for two months after union, in later days of age all will remain.
1945.nuance: The verse is obscure. உருப்பெற்று may mean gaining a firm body. One reading: restraint after union keeps strength into old age. Another: the effects of the union remain even if one later abstains.

1946.reading: There is no harvest for the high except for those who sow, no knowledge for the eminent except for those who sow; if they come to know the seed within the seed, it is a mango in the churning-stick.
1946.nuance: வித்து (seed) is bindu, so 'those who sow' may be those who give bindu its proper end, or those who plant it upward in yoga. வித்தினில் வித்து (the seed in the seed) is the Lord, as in 1931. மத்தில் இருந்ததோர் மாங்கனி is obscure; it may mean something sweet hidden in an unlikely place.

1947.reading: In thought are letters, life span and everything; the Lord is in thought with the womb and the life; thought becomes seed, cause and effect; and when thought is cut off, all these are imagination.
1947.nuance: கருத்து (thought, intention) puns on கரு (womb, embryo) in every line. The last line makes the world of seed and birth a construct of thought, which ends when thought ends; this is a reading, not the only one.

1948.reading: When bindu stays unspent, there stay the undying breath, great strength, power, unfailing intellect, tapas, japa and silence; and when bindu is dried up within, undying siddhi comes.
1948.nuance: ஒழியாத and அழியா alternate down the lines. விந்து வற்றிலே may mean 'when bindu is dried up', burnt within as 1949 describes, not 'when it runs dry' by loss; the first reading fits the chapter.

1949.reading: To dry it, kindling the fire, turning it back and raising it, plugging the whirling fire and reaching the light, those who drink, step by step, the nectar of the full moon are the Siva-yogis.
1949.nuance: The fire at the root is raised (மறித்தேற்றி), the whirl (சுழி) is sealed, and the moon at the head yields nectar: the standard sequence of Tirumular's kundalini yoga as tradition reads it.

1950.reading: Yogi, jnani, excellent siddha, the yogi who is lord of jnana, and one who, though passion comes, drinks the nectar in due order: such is the noble one whose bindu does not perish.
1950.nuance: மோகம் உறினும் (even if passion arises) includes the householder who unites but keeps bindu by method, alongside the yogi and the jnani.

1951.reading: With the Lord as the body, the fire-bindu and the breath-bindu that dies in the earth, bound and mixed in the fire with the eye and burnt, become nectar when eaten and knowledge to the yogi.
1951.nuance: The two bindus are named again in 1965 and 1966 as food and breath. மண்ணிடை மாய்க்கும் may mean the breath that dies in the earth element at the root, or the bindu lost on the ground; கண்ணும் is unclear.

1952.reading: Because they perish without knowing, daily they are ruined through the senses and lament; as knowledge, staying gathered in waking so as to reach the beyond, union will come.
1952.nuance: நனவில் அதீதம் (the beyond-state in waking) is the Siddhanta turiyatita reached while awake. வாயுமே may be the breath or the verb 'it will be attained'; both are possible.

1953.reading: If one thinks of women as Death come to kill, the desire that grew from love falls away; there is no dying even in a hundred crore years, and within the light comes the time free of fault.
1953.nuance: The verse prescribes a way of seeing, not a judgment on women as such: the meditation turns desire off. Sengalvaraya notes a Tiruppugazh parallel where young women's charms take lives as Death does.

1954.reading: The one who has mastered bindu, see, has passed beyond time; the one who wasted bindu passed through time and perished; those who waste bindu through the ages do not know the mingling that came by the breath.
1954.nuance: செற்றவன் means both 'one who subdued' and 'one who destroyed'; the verse uses the same word for the yogi and the waster, and the reading depends on the contrast. காரிகை (woman) and காலின்கண் (by the breath, or at the feet) are unclear.

1955.reading: If you want love's good on the day before union, first clear the woman's belly of waste, cold and bile by fitting remedies, and then embrace.
1955.nuance: A medical prescription in the humoral terms of Siddha medicine: சீதம் (phlegm, cold) and பித்தம் (bile). Tirumular addresses the man and treats the woman's health as part of the rite.

1956.reading: Driving bindu and nada, rising to the upper place, with the rod along the marked path, drinking the nectar that is milk, if you hold on without clinging, the pride of delusion dies, and that bindu too.
1956.nuance: கோல் (rod) is taken as the spine or the central channel. பற்றறப் பற்றினால் (holding without holding) is a paradox. The last line can also mean that bindu dies to its ordinary course.

1957.reading: Bindu's growth, the full fruit of that growth, its end and loss, the increase that comes by restraint, its gladdening loss and its division by nada: to those who grasp these, bindu becomes victory.
1957.nuance: The verse gives the chapter's title term சயம் (victory) its sense: bindu is conquered by knowing its whole course, not only by holding it. நந்திய நாசம் (a gladdening loss) is unclear.

1958.reading: Bindu, the seed in the root centre, knowing its way by the fire there, raising the endless sun above the throat, becomes cool nectar when it reaches the moon.
1958.nuance: வீசம் is bija, seed. பானு (sun) and சந்திரன் (moon) are the hot and cool poles of the yogic body, and the cool nectar is the moon's. அதிகண்டம் is taken as above the throat.

1959.reading: When bindu, the moon of nectar, is consumed, the stream of nectar runs like fire; since this is the Siva-yoga of nectar, siddhi follows, and the jackfruit grove of nectar comes to the yogi.
1959.nuance: அமுதம் opens every line. அங்கியின் மான (like fire, or the fire's measure) is unclear. பலாவனம் (jackfruit grove) is an image of abundant sweetness.

1960.reading: Knowing the yoga by which bindu does not leave, even when two bodies mingle, the pleasure that does not go there is Siva's pleasure, the true pleasure of the enjoyer; fools embrace women but not so that infatuation dies.
1960.nuance: சிவபோகம் (Siva's enjoyment) is the verse's claim: union in which bindu is kept is itself a spiritual bliss. The last line is compressed; it may also be read 'fools do not embrace with infatuation ended'.

1961.reading: Those joined in yoga, though they turn to women, do not release bindu out of love; those who take hold of women's craving for life waste away, though they seem lovers there, their love a matter of juice.
1961.nuance: உயிராசை (craving of life) may be the woman's desire or the man's lust for her. சாற்றிலே (in the juice) is unclear; it may be the bodily fluids, or a pun on சாற்று (declare).

1962.reading: The bindu spoken of becomes victory by Shakti: kindling the fire raised at the root, with nada through the middle channel that does not run in four directions, holding it, drinking the nectar, one becomes the seed.
1962.nuance: நடுநாடி is the central channel. The last word may be read அருந்த வித்தாம் (drinking it becomes seed) or அருந்தவம் (rare tapas); both fit.

1963.reading: Bindu and nada above, the fire at the root: when the fire that came settles in every hair-root, thought changes and Sivam becomes the self, and bindu dies into seed in the true body.
1963.nuance: மயிர்க்கால் தோறும் (in every hair-root) pictures the fire pervading the whole body. சிவம் அகமாக may be 'Sivam as the self' or 'Sivam within'. மெய்க்காயம் (true body) is taken as the body made imperishable.

1964.reading: One who pounds the seed and eats it does not know the harvest; one who, without pounding it, roasts the seed and eats is no different from him in the end; one who, not pounding and eating, sowed the seed is the other.
1964.nuance: A riddle on வித்து. Plainly: to eat the seed is to lose the crop. Symbolically, spending bindu in pleasure or burning it without method both waste it, while the sower turns it to growth. Which practice each figure stands for cannot be fixed.

1965.reading: Seeing how bindu is contained in food, turning back the bindu that is the abiding breath, releasing the lightning-like bindu into the end of nada, the coloured holy bindu dies in the body.
1965.nuance: அன்னம் may mean food or the swan (the breath, hamsa); with பிராணன் it gives the two bindus of 1966. நாதாந்தம் is the end of nada. 'Dies in the body' is taken as being absorbed, not lost.

1966.reading: For those who know the two bindus called food and breath, take them in and can practise, a golden form appears with the eight siddhis, and all such stand beyond destruction.
1966.nuance: சொன்னமாம் உரு (a golden form) is the perfected body of the siddhas. எண்சித்தி are the eight great powers. As in 1965, அன்னம் may be food or the hamsa breath.

1967.reading: The letter Si standing as the breath one thinks on, the letter Ma joining, these one with the three, go to Parashakti; to tell how to join with bindu's victory is the teaching.
1967.nuance: சிகாரம் and மகாரம் are letters of the five-syllable mantra. ஒருமூன்றோடு ஒன்ற (one with the three) may be the three remaining letters or the three bodies. உபதேசம் is the guru's teaching.

1968.reading: It is itself the teaching, and there is nothing apart from it; when the fourteen that came from bindu, high as the sky, subside like deer, then intellect and the nature of the Siva-state come.
1968.nuance: பதினான்கு (fourteen) may be the fourteen worlds or the fourteen instruments (ten senses and four inner faculties). மானேர் (like deer) is unclear.

1969.reading: As bindu and nada bore fruit, these many lives came forth; for all abiding lives the end and the beginning, and the mantras too, are that; when bindu is contained, Sivoham grows.
1969.nuance: சிவோகம் (I am Siva) is the experience of identity with Siva. The verse joins the cosmic bindu that brings forth lives (1923) to the bodily bindu whose containment brings Sivoham.

1970.reading: The way of roasting, the way of weighing the mind's victory, the way of sticking to that long mountain and sealing it, and the way of cutting that evil karma.
1970.nuance: Line 4 repeats the end of line 3 and the verse has no main verb, so the conclusion is lost. வறுக்கின்ற (roasting) echoes 1964's roasted seed; நீள்வரை (the long mountain) may be the spine.

1971.reading: If bindu and nada join together and meet the moon, the nectar of the beautiful sky will spring there, and the mantra uttered there becomes the oblation.
1971.nuance: சுந்தர வானம் (the beautiful sky) is taken as the space in the head. The last line turns the inner act into the fire rite: mantra and oblation happen within.

1972.reading: Mind with its essence, mind and ear: those of one kind rise and agree in the channel; the word rising in the mind is speech, and if one seeks that desire, it is heavy juice.
1972.nuance: The verse is obscure. It may trace sound from mind to speech, and then say that desire turns this power into gross fluid (இரதம்).

1973.reading: They do not know the place where sound, the mind of sound and the mind's thought agree and know; for those who know truly the place where knowing happens, that very place is the Father's abode.
1973.nuance: அத்தன் (Father) is the Lord. The verse places the Lord at the point where knowing itself takes place, not in an outer object of knowledge.

1974.reading: From chest to feet is earth, at the navel water, below the breast fire, below the hands above the dark mountain air, and the beauty mingled above is space.
1974.nuance: The five elements are placed in regions of the body. The boundaries (உரம் அடி, கருமலை, கைக்கீழ்) are not clear, and the order of regions in the verse may be disturbed.

links.note: 1936 laments that people do not know how bindu is lost or how to guard it; 1948 lists what stays when it is kept: breath, strength, intellect, tapas, japa, silence and siddhi.

Both give the same sequence: kindle the fire at the root, raise it through the sealed central way, and drink the nectar. 1949 calls those who do it Siva-yogis; 1962 calls it bindu's victory by Shakti.
1946 says there is no harvest except for the sower; 1964 turns this into a riddle of three men who pound, roast or sow the seed, and only the sower is apart.
1933 traces food into body and mind, and 1934 into bindu; 1966 names the bindu of food and the bindu of breath and makes knowing both the way to the golden body.
1923 makes cosmic bindu the source of powers, gods and speech; 1969 makes bindu and nada the source of all lives and mantras, and then turns to the bodily bindu whose containment brings Sivoham.
Both see woman as கூற்று, Death. In the Kural the lover discovers it, struck by her eyes; Tirumular makes it a deliberate meditation that ends desire and with it death.

The Naladiyar quells desire by taking the woman's body apart into entrails and blood. Tirumular does not reject union: kept with bindu unspent, it is Siva's own pleasure, and only the fool's infatuation is condemned.

Kural 148 calls not looking at another man's wife (பிறன்மனை நோக்காத) the great manliness of the worthy. 1937 asks the yogi to leave without looking at the women he sees (பார்க்கின்ற மாதரைப் பாராது அகன்று) and to lay waste the eye's desire. The Kural's rule of conduct about one class of women becomes in 1937 a discipline of the eye toward all, turned to the root centre.

Kural 360 says pain perishes when even the names of காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம் perish. 1938 says one who harbours காமாதி (lust and its kin) lives in fear (உட்கும்), and that Siva-yoga does not stay without grace. Both name the same triad as the root of suffering; 1938 adds that removing it is grace's work before technique's.

830 fixes the measure of paryanka yoga in nazhigai within one act of union (அஞ்சு கடிகைமேல் ஆறாங் கடிகையில்). 1939 extends the timing to the lunar calendar, naming days in the waxing and waning fortnights (வளர் பக்கம், அபரம்) for those who go into a woman's power. Together they show the yogic treatment of union as governed by time at both scales.

790 assigns the breath to the left or right side by weekday and by waxing or waning fortnight. 1941 says the act is to be done when the moon and sun breaths weaken (இந்து பருதிகால் நையுமிடத்து), leaving right and left (வலம் இடம் தீர்ந்து). 790's regime of alternating sides is the ordinary order; 1941 names the moment that order is suspended, as the breath leaves both channels.

837 says those who keep the intent mingled feel no strain (வருத்தமும் இல்லை) even when sharing themselves with a woman, and the silver rises unflagging. 1942 asks for one who stays unshaken (நடுங்காது இருப்பான்) as the senses press, letting go clinging to the woman while holding the breath. Both locate the discipline inside union rather than in abstaining from it.

826 says that when enjoyment is willed the breath does not leave (போகாது வாயுவும்) and the silver turns back from passion. 1943 has the lover speak endearments and then, at the moment of release, watch the faculty go within (கண்ட கரணம் உட்செல்ல). Both describe the same practice of the breath turned inward at the height of union.

1944 says the times that came into play at union determine the child's life span, death day and qualities (கட்டிய வாழ்நாள் சாம்நாள் குணம்). 453 says that at the hour of love the Lord, present in the house of bondage, fixes the span and the earthly life (பண்புறு காலமும் பார்மிசை வாழ்க்கையும்). 453 places in the Lord's act what 1944 reads off the calendar of union.

1947 says thought becomes seed, cause and effect, and that when thought is cut off these are கற்பனை (imagination). 2505 places the Supreme in the void beyond காரிய காரணம் கற்பனை (imagined effect and cause). Both call the chain of cause and effect a construct; 1947 ties its end to the cutting of thought.

477 says the embryo's form seen as male, female or neither (ஆண்பெண் அலியெனுங் கற்பனை) is fashioned by the Light's power. 1947 puns கருத்து on கரு and says that, when thought is cut, womb, seed and life span are கற்பனை. The same word for the embryo's fashioning is in 477 the Lord's making and in 1947 the mind's.

1948 says that when bindu stays unspent the undying breath, strength, intellect, tapas, japa and silence stay, and siddhi comes. Thiruppugazh 709 asks for the bindu that books and creeds cannot give (பேசிக்கொடாத விந்து) made steady as the light of truth, with the breath in the nose turned into the skull. Both join kept bindu and turned breath as the yogic way past what learning gives.

1950 counts among those whose bindu does not perish one who drinks the nectar in order even though passion comes (மோகம் உறினும்). 1904 says one keeping to the path open to people on earth (புவியோர் நெறி) advances in Siva-yoga by way of bindu. Both open the bindu discipline to the householder, not only the renouncer.

1951 speaks obscurely of a fire-bindu and a breath-bindu (பிராணனாம் விந்து) burnt together into nectar and knowledge. 1966 names the two bindus plainly as அன்னம் and பிராணன் and says those who know them gain a golden form and the eight siddhis. 1966 gives the terms that make 1951 readable.

1952 says people perish through the senses unknowing, and that the beyond is to be reached in waking (நனவில் அதீதம்). 2159 says turiya lies within waking itself (துரியம் இருப்பதும் சாக்கிரத்து உள்ளே). Both refuse to place the highest state apart from the waking life where the senses ruin people.

841 says those who in union can join self with self may live on earth for many ages (மண்ணிடைப் பல்லூழி வாழலும் ஆமே). 1954 says the one who has mastered bindu has passed beyond time (காலம் கடந்தவன்), while the waster passed through time and perished. 1954 turns 841's long life into escape from time itself, and adds the waster's contrast.

481 says that if the mother's belly is heavy with waste (மாதா உதரம் மலமிகில்) the child is dull, with water mute. 1955 tells the man to clear the woman's belly (நாரி உதரக் கலத்தின் மலத்தை) of waste, cold and bile before union. 1955 prescribes the remedy whose reason 481 gives.

Kural 941 says the three humours the learned count, beginning with wind (வளிமுதலா எண்ணிய மூன்று), cause disease in excess or lack. 1955 names சீதம் and பித்தம் with waste as what must be removed before union. The same humoral medicine that the Kural applies to daily health Tirumular applies to conception.

Kural 350 says: cling to the clinging of the one without clinging, in order to let clinging go (பற்றுக பற்று விடற்கு). 1956 says that if one holds without clinging (பற்றறப் பற்றினால்) the pride of delusion dies. Both turn the word பற்று against itself: a holding that frees from holding.

Kural 122 says to guard restraint as wealth, for life has no greater gain (ஆக்கம்) than அடக்கம். 1957 names among the things one must know about bindu அடக்கத்தில் ஆக்கமும், the increase that comes by restraint. The same pairing of restraint and gain, ethical in the Kural, is bodily in Tirumular.

1491 says both yoga and enjoyment (யோகமும் போகமும்) belong to the yogi who does not perish. 1960 says that when two bodies mingle with bindu kept, the pleasure is சிவபோகம், the true pleasure of the enjoyer, while fools embrace without ending infatuation. 1960 shows how 1491's union of yoga and bhoga is meant: within the act of union itself.

828 says that in bodily union one who guards bindu so it is not spoiled (பங்கப் படாமற் பரிகரித்து) becomes lord. 1961 says those joined in yoga, though they turn to women, do not release bindu out of love, while those who take hold of craving waste away. Both make the keeping of bindu within union the line between the yogi and the one who is drained.

1963 says the fire from the root settles in every hair-root (மயிர்க்கால் தோறும்) as Sivam becomes the self. 2856 says nectar wells up at every hair-root (மயிர்க்கால் தோறும் அமுதூறிய) in a bliss beyond difference. The same figure of the whole body pervaded marks in one the yogic fire and in the other the realised bliss.

1934 traces how food becomes chyle and, through the seven bodily elements, a drop of bindu like dew on grass. 1965 starts from there, seeing how bindu is contained in food (அன்னத்தில் விந்து அடங்கும்), and turns it back and releases it to the end of nada. 1934 is the physiology; 1965 is the practice built on it.

1095 tells one to take the letter Sa first and, for the teaching of the breath (வாசிப் பிராணன் உபதேசம்), join it with the bindu. 1967 sets the letter Si as the breath (சிகாரம் ... பிராணனாய்) and calls joining bindu's victory the உபதேசம். Both bind a mantra letter, the breath and bindu into one guru-given teaching.

1968 says the fourteen that came from bindu subside like deer (பதினான்கு மானேர் அடங்க) before the Siva-state comes. 2159 says the fourteen jackals ate poison and died (நரிகள் பதினாலு நஞ்சுண்டு செத்தன) and turiya is reached within waking. Both figure the fourteen faculties as animals whose stilling opens the highest state.

1971 repeats 961 almost word for word: bindu and nada join, meet the moon, nectar wells up, and the mantra uttered there becomes the oblation (ஆகுதி). Only அந்தர வானத்து becomes சுந்தர வானத்து. The near-repeat sets the bindu chapter's nectar teaching inside the earlier chakra chapter's rite.

source_issues: 1970: line 4 repeats the end of line 3 (அப் பொல்லா வினையை) and the verse has no main verb; the closing line seems lost.
1939, 1940: the day counts (மேல்பனி மூன்றிரண்டு, ஆறுஐந்து பன்னொன்றும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1946 line 4 (மத்தில் இருந்ததோர் மாங்கனி) and all of 1972 are obscure and may be corrupt.
